background: Svenska Handelsbanken is a Swedish bank run on a decentralised branch model, funded by Swedish deposits and covered bonds and lending mainly on residential mortgages and to businesses in Sweden, Norway, the UK and the Netherlands.
synthesis: Ratings are among the highest in Europe: AA on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at AA-, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is mixed against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 17.2% is above the peer median but has fallen 1.1 points since 30 Jun 2025, while leverage of 4.2% is in the bottom quarter, as is usual for a mortgage-heavy Nordic bank. Liquidity is also mixed, with LCR of 186% in the top quarter and NSFR of 122% a little under the peer median. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days; a conservative lender with a long record of low credit losses, which the ratings reflect.
